title: Zendesk client identifiers, subdomains and placeholder Bearer or client_secret values
summary: A client identifier and subdomain, the documented Authorization: Bearer {access_token} template, a scheme-only header, and Bearer or client_secret values that are placeholders, environment references or masked displays.
rationale: The client identifier and the subdomain are public-facing configuration, not credentials. The documented template with braces around the word access_token marks where a value goes and holds none, a scheme with no value has nothing to protect, a reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, and a masked display has no recoverable value. Protecting any of these would redact text a reader needs.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are identifiers, placeholders, references, masked text or non-secret outputs, not credential values. That a placeholder or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Zendesk statement.

sources.supports: Zendesk supports using OAuth access tokens to authenticate API requests. ... An OAuth token gives access to a single Zendesk instance ... Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Identifier: Used as client_id in API requests. Secret: Used as client_secret in API requests. This is shown only once after saving, so store it safely.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
